newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Hebron road opens to Palestinians after 3 years.
newsitem.headline: Hebron road opens to Palestinians after 3 years.

text.p: Israel opened a main road in Hebron to Palestinian traffic for the first time in three years on Monday under a U.S.-brokered Israel-PLO deal signed last month, witnesses said.

They said ambulances, taxis and municipal vehicles began trickling through the section of Shuhada -- or Martyrs -- street which Israeli security forces opened to traffic in the West Bank town around 7.30 a.m. (0530 GMT).
Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to PLO rule on January 17. The street borders Jewish settlements in the 20 percent of Hebron still under Israeli control.

The street, closed to Palestinian vehicles since a Jewish settler massacred 29 Arabs kneeling in prayer at al-Ibrahimi mosque in February 1994, will gradually reopen over a four-month period under the peace deal.

Palestinians had demanded the reopening of the street which abuts an old vegetable market. Some 400 Jewish settlers, who opposed the Hebron handover, and 20,000 Arabs live on the Israeli-held side of the volatile town.

"It is a new reality, a problematic reality," settler spokesman Noam Arnon told Israel Television minutes before the opening. "It will be flooded with Arab cars which will pose a real danger to the Jews here."
